clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old farmer with heavy smoking history presented with a 10-month history of productive cough, yellowish sputum, moderate hemoptysis, altered general condition, and feverish symptoms. Clinical exam revealed left hemithorax dullness, hypoxia, and bilateral axillary adenopathies. Chest X-ray showed hydro-pneumothorax. Pleural puncture yielded chocolate-colored purulent fluid. Direct microscopic examination of the pleural fluid showed numerous filamentous gram-positive bacilli suggestive of Actinomyces. The search for tuberculosis (BK and GeneXpert MTB/RIF) in pleural fluid and sputum was negative. Biological work-up revealed inflammatory syndrome, anemia, leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, and HIV-negative status. Chest CT scan showed a left lung abscess communicating with bronchi and left pyopneumothorax communicating with the abscess, along with infectious micronodules in the right lung. The diagnosis of pulmonary nocardiosis was confirmed by the bacteriological study of the pleural fluid after direct examination and positive culture for Nocardia species.
